chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Talhah ibn Zayd from his father from Ali (peace be upon him) that he said:
There is no 'Arafah except in Mecca, and there is no harm in them gathering in the cities on the Day of 'Arafah to supplicate to Allah.

key_terms.الْأَمْصَارِ: The cities (plural of miṣr), referring to urban centers where pilgrims may gather
key_terms.بِمَكَّةَ: In Mecca, indicating the specific location required for the ritual of 'Arafah
key_terms.عَرَفَةَ: The station of 'Arafah, a pivotal ritual site and day in Hajj
key_terms.يَدْعُونَ اللَّهَ: They supplicate to Allah, referring to the act of du'a

ai.seo_question: Can pilgrims perform du'a on the Day of 'Arafah outside of Mecca?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ali (AS) clarifies the distinction between the essential pillar of Hajj (wuquf at Arafah) and the recommended act of supplication, establishing that while the physical presence at the specific station is mandatory for validity, the spiritual act of du'a can be performed collectively in other cities. This ruling provides flexibility for pilgrims and underscores the Shia scholarly view that the core requirement is the intention and presence at the designated time, allowing for communal worship outside the immediate vicinity of the Mount.
